name: pair_device
description:
Add/pair or remove a physical device -- callable any time.

ADDING A NEW DEVICE -- ask in this order, QR code FIRST, protocol only as a fallback:
1. Ask the customer whether they have a QR code to scan (or a pairing/setup code to type in instead). If yes: call include with scan_qr_code: true (or raw_code set) plus client_id -- omit protocol entirely, it is not needed for this path and must not be asked for. Works for insteon/zwave/matter; never relevant for zigbee in practice (a zigbee device never has a QR code in this system, so this question alone already rules it out -- don't ask protocol to find that out).
2. Only if they say no, THEN ask which protocol, and follow the per-protocol procedure below: zwave/zigbee -> include with protocol set, no code. insteon -> ask whether they know the device's own address; yes -> add_by_address, no -> include with protocol: insteon, no code (linking mode). matter -> a QR/pairing code is mandatory -- this is really step 1's question asked specifically for Matter (there is no manual fallback), not a new one.

PROTOCOL (the `protocol` argument -- lowercase: insteon, zwave, zigbee, matter, x10):
- Omit it entirely for step 1's QR-code path above. For the step-2 fallback, x10 returns a not-yet-supported message -- walk the customer through manual pairing instead.
- Removing an EXISTING device: never guess its protocol from the device's name or model. Call get_device_family (INSTEON -> insteon, Z-Wave -> zwave, Zigbee -> zigbee, Matter -> matter), or just try node_op(delete): it succeeds for insteon and is rejected for zwave/zigbee/matter/plugin with the real protocol named in the error (see DEVICES, Protocol family).
- A Z-Wave controller still running the Legacy (pre-Z-Matter) generation returns a clear error for any zwave action -- tell the customer to use eisy-ui for that controller.

ACTIONS:
- add_by_address (insteon/x10 only -- the only protocols with a customer-readable address, and only reachable once protocol is already known -- see step 2 above): for a device whose own address the customer already knows or can read off the unit. The bare three hex byte pairs printed on the device (e.g. 'AA BB CC') is all that's needed -- never ask the customer for a trailing button/group number just to pair it; the system defaults that to the device's main group automatically (see device_address). One address can enumerate more than one hub-side node -- every one actually added is collected, not just the first. Waits (up to ~60s per node enumerated) for every one of them to actually become usable before returning, so it's safe to reference the returned device_address (the first/primary one) in the very next tool call; new_devices lists every address+name actually added, same shape as include's own new_devices below.
- include: always dismisses any stale discovery dialog first automatically (no argument needed, transparent) before doing anything else. Then: 
  - protocol omitted (step 1's QR-code-first path, protocol genuinely not known yet): scan_qr_code/raw_code + client_id are required; this opens eisy-ui's QR-scan dialog on the customer's own screen and waits for a new device to appear, returned in new_devices -- the result omits protocol too, since it's genuinely unknown (resolve it afterward via get_device_family if it's ever needed).
  - zigbee (protocol known -- step 2): no further question -- call it immediately, in this same turn, with no clarifying question or confirmation first. zwave/matter devices likewise have no customer-readable address, so add_by_address is never valid for them either.
  - matter/zwave, and insteon once the customer has said they want linking mode (not add_by_address), with protocol already known: ask whether the customer has a QR code to scan (set scan_qr_code: true) or a pairing code/setup code/device address to type in instead (set raw_code to it) -- either opens eisy-ui's QR-scan dialog on the customer's own screen (requires client_id) and waits for a new device to appear, returned in new_devices the same way as above. In practice this question should already have been answered by step 1 before protocol was even asked -- reaching this with protocol known but no QR answer yet means step 1 was skipped and should be asked now instead of defaulting.
  - matter with NEITHER a QR code nor any other code: there is no manual fallback -- returns a message saying a QR/pairing code is required, with no on-hub action taken.
  - zwave/insteon with NEITHER a QR code nor any other code: opens the hub's own manual pairing/linking mode and waits for that protocol's own pairing session to end (however long the customer takes), then returns whatever was newly discovered in new_devices (address + whatever name the hub assigned, usually blank -- no separate lookup needed; rename via node_op using that address). insteon's linking-mode window stays open for a full 5 minutes (not the ~80s every other wait in this tool uses) specifically so the customer can link several devices one after another -- say so to the customer before calling (see the blocking-call note below). device_type is optional -- omit it unless the customer already volunteered it.
- exclude (zwave/zigbee/matter only -- insteon has no distinct hardware remove mode; use node_op(delete) for insteon): requires protocol -- never valid for the no-protocol QR path. Also dismisses any stale discovery dialog first automatically. Removes a device. Whether device_address is required depends on the protocol -- this is the one place add/remove aren't symmetric, so don't assume. For zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL and should normally be omitted -- the customer identifies the device physically (pressing its own exclude button once the hub is listening), not by name in chat, so never ask 'which device' first; this opens removal mode, waits (same ~80s budget) for the customer to activate the device, then reports which device the hub excluded in removed_devices. Only pass device_address for zwave if the customer already volunteered a specific address. For zigbee/matter, device_address IS required (from DEVICE DATABASE, never guessed) and there is no physical activation window: the call performs the ENTIRE removal immediately and returns status=exclusion_committed with removed_devices already populated -- do not tell the customer to do anything on-screen, and do not call this twice; one call is the whole operation. Zigbee can fail silently at the network layer (the hub only disables the node locally); this call detects that and returns an error (with device_address) instead of a false success -- if you get it, tell the customer the device could not be removed from the Zigbee network and they need to remove it manually from the eisy-ui interface, linking it as /nodes/{device_address} per UI NAVIGATION.

BEFORE CALLING include or a zwave exclude: these BLOCK waiting for the customer's own physical action (or dialog interaction), which they do on their own screen, not in this chat -- up to ~80s for every path except insteon's no-code linking mode (5 minutes, see above). Say your instructions to the customer as plain text in this same reply, immediately BEFORE the tool call (e.g. 'I've put the hub in pairing mode -- follow the instructions on your screen to add the device.', or for insteon's 5-minute window specifically, 'I've put the hub into linking mode -- you have up to 5 minutes, so press the Set button on each Insteon device you want to add, one after another.') -- never 'let me know when you're done' or any variant expecting a chat reply, because there won't be one; the call already waits for that to finish on its own. Text written after the tool call in your reply is what you say once it's already done.

LINKING: any device this tool adds/pairs/removes, regardless of protocol, is a device node -- when you mention it in your reply, link it as /nodes/{address} per UI NAVIGATION, using the address this tool's own result gave you (e.g. new_devices[].address). Never a /plugins/... link -- that is only ever for the plugin marketplace/dashboard/licenses, never for a device (even one a plugin created). For adding a marketplace plugin (not a physical device), use install_plugin/buy_plugin instead.

protocol.description: The device's protocol family, lowercase. OMIT this entirely for action=include when the customer has a QR code/pairing code to scan (scan_qr_code/raw_code set) -- ask about that FIRST, before protocol, and only ask protocol as a fallback once they say they don't have one. Required for every other case: add_by_address, exclude, and a bare (non-QR) include. Removing an existing device: from get_device_family (INSTEON -> insteon, Z-Wave -> zwave, Zigbee -> zigbee, Matter -> matter) or a rejected node_op(delete) -- never guessed from the device's name.

action.description: add_by_address is insteon/x10 ONLY (needs protocol + device_address) -- not valid for zwave/zigbee/matter, which have no customer-readable address before pairing; only reachable once protocol is already known (the customer said they don't have a QR code, then said they know the device's address). include (add): always dismisses stale discovery dialogs first automatically. With protocol omitted (the customer has a QR code/pairing code and was asked about it before protocol at all), scan_qr_code/raw_code + client_id are required and protocol is skipped entirely. With protocol given: zigbee goes straight to the bare protocol-level include call. matter/zwave, and insteon once linking mode is chosen, ask about a QR code (scan_qr_code) or pairing/setup code/device address (raw_code) first -- either opens eisy-ui's QR-scan dialog (needs client_id) and waits for a new device; with neither, matter errors (no fallback) while zwave/insteon fall back to manual linking mode (insteon's own window is 5 minutes, not ~80s). exclude (remove) requires protocol -- works for zwave/zigbee/matter only -- also dismisses stale discovery dialogs first automatically; for zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL (the customer identifies the device physically, not by name -- opens removal mode and blocks the same way as include); for zigbee/matter, device_address IS required and it performs the whole removal in this one call, immediately, no window.

device_address.description: Required for action=add_by_address, and for action=exclude when protocol is zigbee/matter. For add_by_address: the three hex byte pairs printed on the device itself (e.g. 'AA BB CC') -- the device is brand new and isn't in DEVICE DATABASE yet, so there is nothing to copy from there. Never ask the customer for a trailing button/group number to pair it; the system defaults it to the device's main group (1) automatically. Only include a different trailing number yourself if the customer explicitly names a specific different button/group on a multi-button device. For action=exclude when protocol is zigbee/matter: the exact address shown in DEVICE DATABASE for that existing device (that exact address is removed directly) -- never guessed. NOT required for action=exclude when protocol is zwave -- omit it there; the customer identifies the device physically and the hub reports back which one was excluded.

device_type.description: Optional device-type hint (add_by_address/include). Never ask the customer for this before calling -- omit it unless they already mentioned the device type unprompted; it is not worth delaying the call for.

scan_qr_code.description: include only, matter/zwave/insteon (never zigbee): set true when the customer has a QR code to scan visually in eisy-ui's dialog, with nothing to type. Ask about this BEFORE asking protocol at all -- protocol can (and should) be omitted entirely when this is set. Leave raw_code unset in this case. Requires client_id. Defaults to false.

raw_code.description: include only, matter/zwave/insteon (never zigbee): a pairing code, setup code, or device address the customer typed instead of scanning a QR code -- passed through verbatim to eisy-ui's dialog, which validates/interprets it itself. Ask about this (or scan_qr_code) BEFORE asking protocol at all -- protocol can (and should) be omitted entirely when this is set. Setting this also opens the QR-scan dialog, same as scan_qr_code. Requires client_id.

client_id.description: Required whenever scan_qr_code or raw_code is set. Copy it verbatim from the clientId field of the <ui_context> block already present in this conversation -- never ask the customer for it or invent it.
